name: Bright Lavender
lede: Bright Lavender is a vivid violet built from "bright" plus lavender, first recorded by the 2010 xkcd survey and again by the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary.

sections.title: A modifier that drifts from its base
sections.body:
The name is built the usual way, "bright" plus [[lavender]], first recorded by the 2010 xkcd survey and again by the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary, which places it in block 210 as a vivid violet [1][2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[easter-purple]], [[heliotrope]], [[lighter-purple]] and [[bright-violet]], at 3.3, 6.2, 6.4 and 6.4 ΔE [1].

That gap is the point of calling a color "bright": raising the saturation of a pale name can carry the result into a different part of the color wheel entirely. Siblings here are [[lavender]], [[magenta]], [[purple]], and [[violet]], the points this color sits between [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this vivid violet covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. A hue this saturated at this lightness is outside the range synthetic-era pigments typically hold once aged and varnished, let alone the natural dyes earlier painters had [3].
